svg.text: Base shapes: two shapes (square, triangle), one edge length
Every working edge (face F, laterals R and L) is exactly one unit long, so any edge can bond to any edge. Larger forms come from combinations and sequences.
A. Two base shapes, one edge length
bend Z: turns 60° the other way, face inside
K back (structure seed) — square only; Z has two unit sites
Pairing complements: S↔S (a domino), T↔Z (a side-2 triangle).
A Z is built in place from supplied triangles; square⇄triangle switching is optional (supply balancing).
All turns are 60° steps, so parts share a few directions and fit together.
B. Welded shapes: bonded combinations (and can be split)
The trapezoid is one of many welded shapes. Edge-to-edge bonds pinned at both corners are rigid;
one pinned corner would make a hinge.
C. A bent chain is copied by complementary shapes, so the copy is bent too
Each copy unit docks face to face; neighbouring copy units must share whole laterals. Template dark outline, copy lighter; one dot per block.
✓ the bend is a mould: 1 triangle docks,
2 fill the notches → rigid side-2 triangle
S-curve: T and Z in one strand
hairpin SSS TTT SSS in a
Released strands keep their shape (no folding rule needed):
